title: Computer Engineering, B.S. (College of Engineering)
notes: University Park. Verified 2026-08-27 against the real EECS department handbook (eecs.psu.edu, 2024-2025 edition, same handbook system as CMPSC's). 'CMPEN 400-Level elective' (x2) is an ENUMERATED handbook list, not free-form 400-level: CMPEN 416/417/454/455/462/471/472/473/475, EE 453/456 -- note it includes EE courses despite the CMPEN-only label. CMPEN 471 was entirely missing from cmpen_catalog.json (added, prereq data not independently verified against a live fetch -- see that entry's own description). 'CMPSC or CMPEN 400-Level elective' (x2): handbook text 'any 400-level CMPSC or CMPEN course, excluding 494/495/496/497/499' -- note CMPEN's exclusion set is five codes (includes 497), unlike CMPSC's own four-code 494/495/496/499 pattern. 'Department List (General Elective)' (x2) wired via the handbook's real denylist (CMPSC 100/101/200/201/203, EE 465, ESL 4, MATH 200/201, PHYS 250/251, CAS 126/283, STAT 401/487, STAT(MATH) 318/414); the handbook's 'MATH below 140' / 'PHYS below 211' / 'STAT below 319 except STAT 200' floor exclusions aren't expressible with this engine's elective_min_level (a floor-only mechanism applied uniformly, not per-department) -- documented gap, not fabricated. No CMPEN-specific Gen Ed domain exclusions found; CMPEN's natural sciences (CHEM 110, PHYS 211/212/214) are all required courses with no open GN slot, so the domain-less GEN ED slots are already correct, and both GHW slots were already correctly wired. CMPEN 270 is modeled as the plain digital-design intro course (the bulletin's 271/275 sequence is a distinct 2-course alternate, not a drop-in substitute, so it isn't listed as an option here) -- CMPEN 270/271/275's real mutual exclusion is enforced via each course's own 'excludes' field in cmpen_catalog.json. CMPEN 362's real concurrent requirement (STAT 301/318/401/414/418) is a catalog data gap (not encoded in cmpen_catalog.json at all) -- this plan's own sequencing (STAT 418 in Semester 5, before CMPEN 362 in Semester 6) already satisfies it in practice regardless. Attempted adding it as a concurrent_groups OR-group directly to CMPEN 362, but reverted: CMPEN 362 is shared by several minors (e.g. CMPENMIN, CYBERCF) whose own plans don't independently guarantee a STAT course lands first, and the full test suite caught real scheduling failures for those minors once the constraint was added -- fixing the catalog for CMPEN's own major plan isn't worth silently breaking unrelated minors outside this review's scope, so left as a documented gap instead. NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED: a live refetch of the current bulletin page timed out during this review (rate-limited) -- the handbook comparison above is complete, but a bulletin-only staleness check (e.g. a renumbered course) wasn't possible; flagged rather than skipped silently. 'etm' marks the gateway courses (Calc I, Physics I) everything downstream depends on. Post-prereq-parser-fix repair (unrelated to the handbook review, left largely as-is): CHEM 110's real catalog prereq is MATH 22, which chains through MATH 21 -- MATH 21/MATH 22 (Semester 2) act as an engine-only fallback for a hypothetical student with no reported math placement (see expand_math_placement in planner_engine.py). Removed 2026-08-27: MATH 3 and MATH 4 (previously in Semester 1), added on the theory that MATH 21 needs MATH 4 needs MATH 3 -- math_catalog.json's own MATH 21 entry has an empty prereq_groups (no prerequisite at all), and MATH 3/MATH 4 are separately hardcoded as unconditionally satisfied everywhere by expand_math_placement regardless of any student input. They were dead weight inflating the plan by 6 phantom credits with zero effect on schedulability (verified via build_full_plan) -- removed.

items.label: MATH 21 (unlocks MATH 22, needed for CHEM 110's real prereq)
